title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 16
paragraphs: But those who lived around Mount Pangaeum and around the Doberes, Agrianes, and Odomantes, and around Lake Prasias itself, were not conquered at all by Megabazus. He did, however, try to remove even those who lived on the lake, whose dwellings were of this sort: a platform fastened together and resting on lofty piles stood in the middle of the lake's water, with a narrow approach from the mainland by a single bridge. The piles supporting the platform were no doubt originally set there by all the members of the community working together, but since then they continue to set them according to the following rule: every man who marries brings three piles for each wife from the mountain called Orbelus and sets them as supports—and each man takes many wives. Their dwellings are arranged like this: each man has his own hut on the platform to live in, with a trapdoor leading through the platform down to the lake; and they tie their infant children with a rope by the foot, for fear they should roll into the water. They feed their horses and beasts of burden on fish; and the fish are so plentiful that if a man opens the trapdoor and lowers an empty basket by a cord into the lake, after waiting only a short while he draws it up again full of fish. Of the fish there are two kinds, and they call them paprax and tilon.
